intro: The last leg of route 1, from the shrine's side gate (where KM1-3 ended) along the shrine's east side, over the side road at the zebra crossing, to the school gate: the end of the route. It is laid out from your KM1-4 picture, in the order of its five lane pictures, for your approval.

Your picture is drawn in depth, unlike KM1-3's row of shop fronts: the bridge runs away from the camera and the stairs climb to the hall. So it is built in layers, each at its own depth and scale: the stone wall along the pavement, the pavilion just behind it, the pond and bridge 3.5 m back, the shrine's grounds (lanterns, stairs, hall, fortune racks, trees) 8 m back. On the school's side: its wall and gate on the street, the green fences behind, the building 33 m back across its sports ground. From the game camera the layers line up as in your picture, and they slide past one another as the kid walks: that is the depth.

Carved from your views: the big ginkgo (KM-G12), the cherry by the gate (KM-G16) and the lotus (KM-G22). The see-through boxes are what is still to come from the lane pictures: the trees along the steps, the shop and house past the crossing.
reference: KM1-4 The Shrine Bridge, the photographic version: the shrine (the pavilion, the lanterns, the arched bridge over the lotus pond, the stairs to the hall, the fortune racks) and the school (its gate, notice board, cherry, building and fences).
strip: Each model at its real size and place, seen through the game camera as the game frames it, the play lane at the front. See-through boxes are what is still to come. The shading is Blender's, not the game's toon look: judge the places, sizes, order and gaps.
decided: The shrine's wall along the pavement is the low stone wall alone (1.1 m), as the build plan has it. In the picture a wooden fence stands on it; at 2 m it would hide the pond and the bridge from the game camera. The fence stays in the picture's grounds, along their back.
The pavilion is a model just behind the wall. It is painted out of the grounds behind it, and the pond is cut out of them, so nothing is drawn twice.
The zebra crossing is over a side road at the shrine's corner (KM1-4d; your picture goes straight from the shrine to the school). Its pedestrian signals are boxes until KM1-4d comes.
The first-graders walk to the same school ahead of the kid, after the crossing, as on KM1-1's lane.
The street lamp the lane prompt puts on the pavement side stands at the wall instead: nothing taller than 0.4 m stands between the camera and the lane (LEARNINGS E10).
The big ginkgo is 20 m tall, as its card says: from the game camera you see its trunk and the underside of its crown, the rest above the screen.
The 3D lotus is built but not placed: the pond layer already has your picture's lotus, and a lotus in front of it would stand on the gravel. It is ready for the other routes' ponds.

Cost (est., docs/PERFORMANCE.md):
  • KM1-4's nine pieces from the picture: 314 triangles in all, one shared 4096 x 2048 texture (about 11 MB with mips in ETC2 with the cut-outs' alpha, about 5 MB in ASTC 6x6).
  • The ginkgo 2,678 triangles, the cherry 2,830, each with a 2048 texture (about 5.6 MB each in ETC2).
  • The kit's poles, lamp and hedges, the side gate and yard from KM1-3: about 9,000 triangles.
In all, about 15,000 triangles standing, and about 35 MB of textures with the shops still to come.
ask: The lane pictures: KM1-4a to e are on the city prompts page, and none has arrived yet. They bring the trees along the steps, the crossing with its signals, and the shop and house before the school.
Anything to move: a place, the order, the length or the play beats.
